<div class="section-cmd"><span class="ps"></span> Bio</div>
I am a Research Associate at the [El-Erian Institute of Behavioural Economics and Policy](https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/centres/el-erian-behavioural-economics/) at the [University of Cambridge](https://www.cam.ac.uk/) and a Postdoctoral Research Associate at [Queens’ College](https://www.queens.cam.ac.uk/).

My research examines how policy, institutions, and information shape technological change and behaviour. I use quasi-experimental methods and natural language processing to study questions in innovation and public economics. My current work focuses on intellectual property, public procurement, and sustainable innovation.

I completed my PhD in Economics at the [University of St Andrews](https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/), where I was supervised by [Prof. Andy Zapechelnyuk](https://www.ed.ac.uk/profile/professor-andy-zapechelnyuk), [Prof. David A. Jaeger](https://research-portal.st-andrews.ac.uk/en/persons/david-a-jaeger/), and [Dr Min Zhang](https://research-portal.st-andrews.ac.uk/en/persons/min-zhang/). Before starting my PhD, I worked as a market analyst and economic researcher.

I also write about the history of invention, with a keen interest in women whose contributions have been overlooked. [This page](posts/memory.html) presents a selection of women patentees active between 1850 and 1950.
